content.title: The Wall Street Journal
content.text: Renee Reynaud CambreSuch important errors of omission here. 1) God. Family. Country. values. 2) Life skills. 3) Academic rigor. 4) Safe environment. 5) Resources to guide and mentor. I have 2 sons in the Honors Scholars program.75John WillmothUnfortunately, this article leaves the impression that the extremely nice facilities are what is driving students to this school. While the facilities are great, it’s more about a good academic and supportive environment that prepares students for post graduation. It is not superficial. There is real substance.75Kevin CairnsAs an Ivy League grad myself and after attending Harvard, UC Berkeley I can say without hesitation that HighPoint is better. The elite schools have lost their way and there is definitely a changing of the guard. I will no longer donate a penny to the elite schools that trained me, everything is going to HighPoint.Jennifer Godwin PepplerAs a veteran HPU parent, I can speak from first hand tangible experience. Sure, the campus is absolutely beautiful and maintained meticulously. There are nice restaurants that not only provide great food, but also serve as a teaching environment on proper etiquette, swimming pools for students to enjoy (no lazy river, as many ill-informed like to say) and beautiful housing options. Oh wait...housing options that are GUARANTEED for all the years the students are there. That's a rarity among most schools. These things are all really nice, but not at all what attracted our daughter and my husband and me to HPU. Much smaller class sizes, phenomenal hands on labs, very accessible professors, a rigorous program, abundance of available resources to help ensure student success, and two incredible internships which both led to pre-graduation job offers. Our daughter was more than prepared for her post graduation life, both professionally and personally. It was absolutely a fantastic ROI for her and for us. For the record, we are far from a wealthy family. We were grateful for the scholarships she received.924Christina SotoOur daughter attends HPU, and trust me, we are not wealthy! She worked very hard in high school, graduating as salutatorian of her class, and received a scholarship to attend HPU's Honors College. She had opportunities to go to other schools with incredible academic reputations. The reason she chose HPU was because of the school's commitment to a well-rounded education and life skills. The admin and faculty truly care about the student succeeding, and the resources available to help the students do that are incomparable to many other schools. She is definitely academically challenged at HPU, something she was familiar with as she had a rigorous academic education prior to college. The networking and opportunities provided through HPU for students looking forward to a successful career place it above other schools. The "God, Family, Country" values come from the top with the leadership of Dr. Quebain, and permeate into everything that is HPU. Do they have incredible perks and a beautiful campus? Absolutely. But HPU is so much more than that.111Janet Lussier CollinsSchools that focus on the student experience provide much more than elite schools and has been the case for many many years. That being said some really smart schools have also decided to focus on the parent experience and that is a really smart financial move that does not take away from the fact that the student comes first.3Alisa Kutlay TuttleHigh Point is so much more than just a beautiful campus for the “rich” (which is not true) The article fails to mention the great education, life skills and how they prepare their students for the real world. They have great opportunities and internships. I know my son is where he is supposed to be. #proudhpumom25Devonnie Aguilar StempI am interested in this school for my son who is currently a high school junior…can someone speak to the “life skills” they receive at HPU? Like what specifically do they do?6Linda ImhoffMy daughter went there 2003-2007. It was cheaper for here to go there and live on campus than to stay home and commute to our local state school. This is before High Point got expensive. Nido came her junior(?) year. She received and excellent education there. History department was fantastic. Now she doesn’t even recognize the place when she visited8Kimberly CravenIt was the one and only place I applied in 2006. What drew me to the school was 1. How well it was taken care of. 2. Everyone is welcoming and very personable 3. Small class sizes 4. The president knew almost all of the students by name - what other school has that? All the “amenities” were just an added bonus. And I come from an average, middle class family.10
